packets.signature: valueAtFrame(ld, prop, frame) -> number[] (length PROP_DIM[prop], motion.js:506-507, pre-span); segmentLeftKey(track, frame) -> key-object | null
packets.responsibility: Lead-in (2635-2638, 4 lines) frames valueAtFrame as 'the ONE new branch on top of the pre-existing rawValueAtFrame, checked first so an enabled-with-error expression still falls through to the exact keyframed/static value it would have shown before expressions existed'. valueAtFrame(ld,prop,frame) (2639-2646, THE public read, exact branch order): (1) `var raw = rawValueAtFrame(ld, prop, frame)` (motion.js:1270, pre-1769/C02-C20a-j) is ALWAYS computed first, unconditionally; (2) `if (hasExpr(ld, prop))` (motion.js:1338, pre-1769) gates the ONLY other branch — hasExpr is true iff `holder.expressions[prop].enabled && holder.expressions[prop].code` are both truthy; (3) inside that gate, `var evaluated = evalExpressionFor(ld, prop, frame, raw)` (C20m, motion.js:2542) is called, passing `raw` itself as the expression's own fallback value (exposed inside the compiled function as its first positional numeric-or-array argument, C20m's own sandbox binding); (4) `if (evaluated !== null) return evaluated` — a non-null expression result WINS over the raw value; (5) otherwise (no expression, OR hasExpr false, OR evalExpressionFor itself returned null on a compile/runtime error, depth cap, or timeout — see C20m's own error paths) falls through to `return raw` at the function's very last line. This ordering is exactly what the lead-in promises: a property whose expression is enabled but currently erroring degrades to the ordinary keyframed/static value, never to a blank/NaN/frozen read. segmentLeftKey(track, frame) (2649-2656): finds the LEFT key of the segment governing `frame` — returns null if the track has fewer than 2 keys (2653, no segment exists yet); returns the second-to-last key if `frame` is at or past the last key's own frame (2654, holds the final segment open past the end); otherwise scans backward from the second-to-last key for the first key whose own `.frame` is `<= frame` (2655); falls back to `ks[0]` if the scan finds nothing (2656, `frame` is before the first key). Explicitly documented (2650-2651) as 'same contract as camera.js's segmentLeftKey, generalized to any track' — camera.js:148 declares an UNRELATED same-named function (`function segmentLeftKey(frame)`, one argument, closes over camera.js's own module-scoped keys array) in camera.js's own IIFE scope; the two are namesakes with matching algorithms, not the same declaration, and camera.js:605/609 call ONLY camera.js's own copy.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: setKeyAtCurrentFrame/setKeyAtFrame called twice at the SAME frame with different values (with and without a curvePoints argument on the second call), then a third call at an EARLIER frame than all existing keys
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: The second call at the same frame MUTATES the existing key's `.v` in place (never creates a duplicate key at that frame) and updates `.curvePoints` ONLY when a curvePoints argument was actually passed on that call; `track.keys.length` stays constant across the two same-frame calls. The third (earlier-frame) call inserts a new key and the whole `track.keys` array ends up frame-ascending sorted afterward, regardless of call order.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: removeKeyAtCurrentFrame called on a frame with no key there, vs. a frame with a key, for both an opacity prop and a non-opacity prop
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: The no-key case leaves `track.keys` byte-for-byte unchanged (same length, same objects) and does not throw. The has-key case removes exactly that one key object (identity-checked via indexOf+splice) and leaves every other key untouched.

proposed_behavioral_fixtures.matrix: toggleAnimated OFF->ON on a property whose displayValueFor differs from its PROP_DEFAULT/staticValue (e.g. 'order' on a mid-stack layer), immediately followed by ON->OFF at a DIFFERENT frame than the one used for ON
proposed_behavioral_fixtures.expected: OFF->ON: the single seed key's `.v` equals displayValueFor's pre-toggle reading, NOT staticValue's/PROP_DEFAULT's flat default, and its `.frame` equals state.currentFrame at the moment of the ON toggle — valueAtFrame immediately after the ON toggle, evaluated at that SAME frame, equals the pre-toggle displayed value (zero visible jump). ON->OFF: motionStatic[prop] equals valueAtFrame evaluated at the CURRENT frame at the moment of the OFF toggle (which may differ from the ON seed value if keys were added between the two toggles), and ld.motion[prop].keys is empty afterward.
